# BRIEF-CONSOLE-LIVE — the console shows work while it is happening

**Status:** DRAFT, dispatch-ready. Authored 2026-08-16 by Waffles.
**Origin:** Tom, 2026-08-16 09:48Z — "I want to be able to see the work that's being done."
**Scope:** the ops console's read surface only. NO server work — both endpoints this brief
consumes are already built, mounted, and (for one of them) already consumed in production by
another client. This is a wiring brief.

## The finding: it is already built and simply not called

Measured at the bytes 2026-08-16, both ends.

**Server end — mounted and reachable, not merely written.**
`crates/aion-server/src/api/http/router.rs`:
```
:378  .route("/workflows/describe",      post(describe_workflow))
:379  .route("/workflows/describe-live", post(describe_live))
:380  .route("/workflows/children",      post(list_children))
:381  .route("/workflows/history",       post(fetch_history))
:386  .route("/workflows/transcripts",   post(list_transcript_streams))
```
Handlers: `crates/aion-server/src/api/http/describe_live.rs:72` (`describe_live`, with
`describe_live_tests.rs` at `:357`) and `children` with `children_tests.rs`.

**Console end — the two live ones are called ZERO times.**
Instrument: `/usr/bin/grep -o` against the asset `index.html` actually references (read the
ref, do not guess from filenames — the assets dir holds SIX `index-*.js` files and picking the
wrong one is the easy error here). Authoritative bundle:
`crates/aion-server/ops-console-embed/assets/index-CMn6AElm.js`, 1,024,025 bytes.

| endpoint | router line | refs in shipped bundle |
|---|---|---|
| workflows/list | — | 1 |
| workflows/describe | :378 | 3 |
| **workflows/describe-live** | **:379** | **0** |
| **workflows/children** | **:380** | **0** |
| workflows/history | :381 | 6 |
| workflows/transcripts | :386 | 5 |

Canary proving the instrument is live against this file: `workflow` → **373**.

**So the console calls four neighbours on the same router and skips exactly the two that show
live work.** It can show you what a run DID. It cannot show you what a run IS DOING.

**Proven-working consumer already exists.** `crates/aion-cli/src/tail.rs:173-182` posts to
`/workflows/children` with a typed `ChildrenRequest`/`ChildrenResponse`. This endpoint is not
speculative infrastructure — it has a live client in the CLI today. Use its types as the
reference shape rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

## What describe-live already gives us (do not rebuild any of this)
Per `describe_live.rs` and `aion-core/src/describe_live.rs`: the current step
(activity id / type / queue / state), the attempt number, a liveness verdict (including a
`NoLiveOwner` case), the intervention capabilities the run actually supports
(`InjectMessage`, `Cancel`), and a transcript window carrying live agent output plus a usage
estimate. Note deliberately: **there is no default transcript tail window** — the caller
names one. That is a design decision, not an omission; R3 respects it.

## Requirements

R1. **Children: a run shows its legs.** A parent run's view lists its child legs from
    `/workflows/children`, each with workflow type, display name, and status. Render live
    status, never a cached snapshot. Reuse the CLI's request/response types as the contract of
    record; if the console's client layer needs its own shape, derive it rather than
    hand-maintaining a second copy (one truth, not two).

R2. **Live step: a running row says what it is doing right now.** For a non-terminal run,
    surface the current step's activity id/type/queue/state and the attempt number from
    `/workflows/describe-live`. A run that is Running and shows nothing is the defect this
    brief closes.

R3. **Liveness is disclosed, including its bad case.** `NoLiveOwner` must be VISIBLE and
    named in the operator's words — a run whose owner is gone looks identical to a busy run
    today, and that is precisely the confusion being removed. The transcript window size is
    CALLER-CHOSEN: pick a value, state it, and make it adjustable; do NOT silently invent a
    default and present it as the truth. No arbitrary caps beyond the window the operator asks
    for.

R4. **Capabilities gate the controls.** Any intervention affordance shown is driven by the
    capabilities the run actually reports. Never render a control the run cannot honour.

R5. **Poll cadence declared, not assumed.** Live views need a refresh rhythm. State the
    chosen cadence and why, and make it stop when the run reaches a terminal state — a
    terminal run must not be polled forever. If a push path exists, prefer it and say so.

R6. **Field proof at the operator's actual surface.** Take a REAL multi-leg run through the
    console in a browser and show: its legs listed, its current step named while it is still
    running, and the view settling correctly when the run goes terminal. Screenshot evidence.
    A passing unit test is not this proof — the whole finding is that the code exists and
    nobody calls it, which no unit test would have caught.

R7. **Standing gates green at final HEAD, single instance.**

## REQUIRED: Check tiers
R1/R2 are mechanical (the call either appears in the shipped bundle or it does not — the same
grep in this brief is the acceptance instrument, re-run against the NEW bundle, with the
canary). R3's liveness disclosure is behavioural and needs the field proof.

## REQUIRED: Census controls
The endpoint table above is the denominator and it must be RE-DERIVED against the rebuilt
bundle, read from `index.html`'s reference, not from a filename. Positive control: the
`workflow` canary (373 today). Negative control: `describe-live` and `children` at 0 BEFORE
the change — capture the before, or the after proves nothing.

## REQUIRED: Numbers
Every count carries its counter. 1,024,025 bytes / 373 canary / the six-endpoint table are MY
measurements at 2026-08-16 against a bundle dated 15 Aug 23:51. Re-derive.

## REQUIRED: Absence claims
"The console never calls describe-live or children" carries its search — instrument, the
bundle path AND how that path was chosen, and the canary — in the delivery report.

## REQUIRED: Refusal surface
R4's rule is a refusal: an unsupported intervention is not offered. Say so where the operator
can see it, rather than hiding the control with no explanation.

## REQUIRED: Timing sensitivity
R5's cadence is timing-shaped. Declare windows in the fixture; do not assert wall-clock
behaviour from a contended box in either direction.

## Hard constraints (estate law)
Worktree only. NEVER push — landing is the dispatcher's re-gate on the final tree. The
console bundle is GENERATED — rebuild it, never hand-edit an asset; a hand-edited bundle is an
automatic reject. No new dotfolders, no daemons, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR override. Final report
states what is NOT done as plainly as what is.

## Done means
R6's browser proof of a real run showing its legs and its live step; the endpoint census
re-derived before and after with the canary; liveness including `NoLiveOwner` visible and
named; no control offered that the run cannot honour; gates green single-instance.

## Note on why this is small
Nothing here is new capability. The server already answers both questions and one answer
already has a working client. Tom asked to see the work being done, and the honest position is
that we built the ability months ago and never called it from the surface he actually looks at.
